problems.memo_sentence: They also note that prior quantum portfolio optimization work has been limited to smaller or approximate variants, positioning their study as extending quantum approaches to more realistic constrained index-tracking settings.
problems.source_evidence: Previous work on quantum portfolio optimization has optimized portfolios of 40, 60, 100 and 500 assets [2–5], as well as introduced additional constraints such as minimum holding period, investment band, group holdings and volatility constraints [4–6]. ... The problem of cardinality-constrained quantum portfolio optimization and index tracking was recently addressed in Ref.[14] and Ref.[5]. In the former it was proposed to use an iterative hybrid-classical quantum algorithm... In the latter the cardinality constraint was formulated directly as QUBO for a quantum annealer but the formulation relied on an upper bound and was not exact...
problems.explanation: The paper distinguishes prior work mainly by problem formulation (iterative vs non-exact cardinality), not by being confined to 'smaller or approximate variants' in terms of scale or general character. The memo overgeneralizes prior work as 'limited to smaller or approximate variants,' which is broader and more negative than what is stated.
